input.add_to_description: Day 21 ~10:00 AM: fooled by Korvash's feigned surrender (nat 20 Deception), he gloated that the Goat's Throat raid was a purchase, not a raid: he paid Gorrak Vael's first debt-loan to have the pass cleared; Dargan and the clan were an 'expense'. entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You shuffle to the door in your hobbles like a man walking to his own hanging. You put your face to the hand-wide gap and call out in Goblin, flat as a nail: Greyshaft's books are honest, honest as the knife at your sister's throat, spoken from a cold heart and a full belly. Come and break this door.

It works. It works better than you had any right to expect. The Foreman, standing a pace behind you, lets out a long breath he must have been holding for an hour. The colour comes back into his face. The knife at Tessa's neck drops a finger's width, and the crossbows at the shutters sag. For the first time since the fight on the stair, the room believes it has won.

"Good," he says, softly, and what comes next you did not ask for. He is talking to himself as much as to you. "Dargan's son. How perfect that it should be you. You look so like him at the pass, did you know? The Goat's Throat was never a raid, Emberhide. It was a purchase. I lent Captain Vael the warband's iron to have that road cleared, because my contract needed it, and your father was an expense. A fine one, and cheap at the price." He smiles a thin tired smile. "Everything is in the book. Everything."

You bring both chained fists down across the lantern on his desk. The glass bursts and the oil goes up in a sheet of flame, a bright yellow wall that rolls across the floor and catches the Foreman's sleeve. He leaps back with a cry, but the fire on his arm goes out as he beats it against his apron. He is alive. The spilled oil burns on the stone between you and the cloaks.

Nobody in the room has moved. The cloaks are staring at the fire. The one at Tessa's wall has stepped back with his blade half raised. Tessa's hairpin turns once, and the lock on her wrist ring clicks open. She rubs her wrist, and her eyes find yours across the flames.

It's your turn. The burning oil will last two rounds. The inner door, with the bedchamber and the chest, is on your far side of the fire, barred but unguarded. The Foreman stands against the desk, with his back to the wall and two hit points. Six cloaks stand on the other side of the flames. Your wrists are in iron, with your ankles hobbled and 1 hit point in your body. What does Korvash do?

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. At the door, through the gap, the sergeant's voice is still bellowing. It's your turn. You are at 1 hit point, in hobbles, with your chained fists free and the lamp-oil fire spreading. entries.text: notebook: updated Find Tessa
Roll death save.

I'm going to say this plainly first: this turn went hard on you, and the dice did not spare Tessa.

You walk to the door in your hobbles like a man who has given up. Through the hand-wide gap you call out in Goblin, flat as a hanged man, that Greyshaft's books are honest, honest as the knife at your sister's throat, and that Dreg can come and break the door. On the last word you swing your chained fists down across the lantern and smash it off the desk. The burning oil takes the Foreman's sleeve, his apron and his hands. He had two hit points left. He dies where he stands, in a pool of fire, without a word.

Dreg misses your meaning. He only hears an honest man's voice, and the pounding on the stair falters.

The room breaks apart. Two of the grey cloaks throw down their weapons. One of them, the lean one, lifts the bar from the door with shaking hands and flees. Tessa, free of her wall-ring, is a breath behind you. The pin has turned in the lock at last. The other four cloaks do not break. A sword takes you across the ribs and you go down, and the room goes dark. Dreg's Tallies pour in as you fall. Gorrak is with them, bandaged and grey. They cut the four cloaks down in less than a minute.

Tessa is hit twice in the same breath by arrows. She is down by the stove with a hairpin still in her fist. Gorrak reaches her. He tries twice to stop the bleeding, and his hands, which have held a mask and a rod and a sword for thirty years, do not know how. She is gone before the third try.

You do not see it. Dreg, kneeling at your side with his thick fingers on your throat, is the one who keeps you from following her.

You wake at noon in the grey light of the ledger-house, on a pallet someone has put under you, with Dargan's ember-red sash somehow folded under your cheek. The chains are off your wrists. Your head is a bell with a crack in it, and you have 1 hit point. The room smells of smoke and burnt oil. The Foreman's body is gone. The shutters are open, and cold clean air is coming through.

Gorrak Vael sits on the floor beside you, unmasked, his burned jaw bare to the daylight. His hands are in his lap, and he is not looking at your face. Beyond him, on the stool by the stove, a shape lies under a grey cloak with the corner of a small rust-red hand showing at the edge. Brun stands at the door with his spear grounded, his eyes red. Krell is propped against the wall with his arm bound. Dreg is at the window, and he turns.

"She died free," Gorrak says. His voice is rasped and quiet, and it does not shake. "No chain on her. She picked her own lock. She would not let go of the pin."

No one else speaks. Somewhere below, the Tallies are raising a sound that is half a roar and half a hymn. The ledger chest stands in the inner chamber, its door open, the scorched book on the desk beside it where someone has set it down. Nobody has touched it since the Foreman fell.

You are at 1 hit point. You have also gained enough experience to reach second level, and when you're ready we'll go through that together. First, there is a room full of people waiting, and a dead sister. What does Korvash do?

entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You walk to the door, shuffling in your hobbles like a beaten man, and call it through the gap in Goblin, flat and loud. Greyshaft's books are honest, honest as the knife at your sister's throat, and you speak from a cold heart and a full belly. Come and break the door.

The Foreman hears the joke in it, and so does the room. He opens his mouth to give an order. Your chained fists come down on the lantern and it breaks across the desk, and burning oil runs over the wood and over his sleeve. He leaps back and beats it out against the wall, hissing, unburnt but shaking, and the spill between him and his guards makes a low wall of flame. That is the last thing you see. A bowstring sings. The shaft takes you in the ribs, and you go down through the floor.

Tessa has the rest of it, and she tells it later, plain and quick, the way she tells everything. The knife at her throat found no purchase. Her wrist was in iron, and she twisted against it and screamed through the door in Goblin and Common, the page is true, they have a knife at me, break it. The braced door lasted another heartbeat. Then Dreg and a dozen Tallies came through it with a roar, the table-brace split in two, and the grey cloaks, six against twenty, died or dropped their swords. Two died. Four knelt. The Foreman did not run. He stood in the middle of his burning rug, with the beads in his hand, and said in his soft voice that he surrendered to the lawful captain of the Iron Tallies. Gorrak, who had walked up the stair behind the door-breakers with his hands still raw from the rope, said nothing at all for a long time.

Dreg knelt over you and found a pulse, and bound the hole in your side with a strip of the Foreman's own apron. It held.

You wake slowly, on a cot of sacking, in grey afternoon light. It is about two in the afternoon of the day after midwinter's eve, and you have 1 hit point. The shutters are open and the wind smells of snow and tin. Your wrists are bare. The iron is gone, and the skin under it is raw to the meat. Dargan's greataxe leans against the foot of the cot with the ember-red sash on the haft, your handaxes and javelins in a bundle beside it. Someone found them in the Foreman's chest.

The ledger-house is scorched and wrecked. The cloaks' bodies have been carried out, and four of them kneel in a corner with their hands bound. Brun stands guard on them, white-faced, with a spear. Krell sits on the floor with his head in a fresh bandage, grinning at you with half his face. The Foreman is bound in his own chair behind his own desk, with a clean shirt and no beads. Beside him, on the desk, lies the scorched ledger with its cover open. No one has touched it.

Tessa sits at your elbow with her hand on your wrist. She is bruised and cut, and she is smiling for the first time since you found her. Gorrak Vael stands at the window with his back to you, his burned face in profile against the snow-light, and the notched rod hangs unused from his belt. Dreg waits at the door.

"He's awake," Tessa says.

Gorrak turns. Whatever he has decided, it is in his one open eye. "The book is yours," he says. "Your sister's too. Burn it, or read it, or hold it up to the miners and let them choose. I have decided nothing, because I owe you the choice. The Foreman is mine to judge, but I will hear you first." He looks at the greataxe. "And your oath to the Tallies is a year and a day of your life that I do not intend to collect. But I'll say that when you have eaten, not before."

Outside, in the yard, the Tin Row's remnants are being fed. The sun is a hand above the ridge, and you have the whole afternoon.

entries.text: notebook: updated Brakk

You drop behind a boulder, out of the archers' line, and shout down your terms. Blades and shields only, at the ford-stones, you and Brakk, and no archers. If you put him down, he and his nine lay down their arms and walk to Harrowmere to answer. If he beats you, your spears go home and the barrel is his.

For a long moment there is only the sound of the stream. Then Brakk laughs, a short dry bark, and the sound of it goes through you. "A big mouth, like the old man's. Done." He lifts his sword hand and the two archers on the roof lower their bows, though they don't unstring them. "Shield and blade. The sergeant may watch, I'd like him to. He should see what he lay in the stones for."

You whistle two notes back toward the gully, and in a few minutes Ushk comes up the goat-path at a jog, helm in hand, with Hale beside him puffing on his staff. Behind them the six Tally spears fan out along the road. Nobody likes this, you can read it in Hale's face. He grips your arm. "He means to cheat. He's a man who cheats. Keep your back to the stream and your eyes on his ten."

You check yourself as you walk down. Your breath is ready in your chest, and your rage waits like a coal. At the foot of the path the three shield-men part to let you through, and none of them looks at you. The ford-stones lie ahead, humped and black, with the cold water running between them. The stones are broad and dry enough to fight on, but flat only in places.

Brakk is already there, on the far side, with his shield on his arm and his ring glinting. He is bigger than you remembered: broad-chested, scarred about the jaw, and every bit as calm as Ushk said. He looks you up and down.

"Whenever you like, boy," he says.

It is a quarter past seven. The ford-stones are ten paces across. Behind Brakk his nine stand in a loose half-circle, and behind you stand Ushk and Hale. Archers hold their bows slack on the roof.

Do you rage as you step onto the stones? What does Korvash do?
